findings.title: add_members/remove_member read params[:group_id] but the routes only provide params[:id]
findings.body: The new routes in config/routes.rb (lines 49-50) are declared as bare `delete "members"` / `put "members"` inside `resources :groups`, which Rails turns into member routes of the form `/admin/groups/:id/members` — the group id arrives in `params[:id]`. However `add_members` (line 66) and `remove_member` (line 85) do `params.require(:group_id)`, and the Ember client (discourse/models/group.js removeMember/addMembers) puts the id only in the URL path, sending only `user_id`/`usernames` in the body. As a result every real request to add or remove a member raises ActionController::ParameterMissing and returns a 400, so both features are completely broken in production. The controller specs don't catch this because they bypass the router and inject `group_id` directly. Either the routes need to expose `:group_id` (e.g. nested/scope) or the controller should use `params.require(:id)`.

findings.title: totalPages is off by one whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit
findings.body: `totalPages` computes `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. For e.g. 100 members with limit 50 this returns 3, although only 2 pages exist (the correct formula is `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`). Because `showingLast` compares currentPage to this inflated totalPages, the "next" button stays enabled on the real last page; clicking it sets offset = user_count, and the server returns an empty list, so the admin lands on a phantom empty page (e.g. "3/3" with no members). This affects every group whose member count is an exact multiple of 50.

findings.title: Public group members list is now truncated to 50 with no pagination UI
findings.body: Previously `members` returned all members for non-automatic groups and only applied a limit (default 200) to automatic ones. The new code applies `limit` (default 50) to every group. The public group members page (discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6 calls findMembers with the model's default limit of 50, and discourse/templates/group/members.hbs has no next/previous controls) therefore now shows only the first 50 members of any larger group, with no way for users to see the rest — a regression from the previous behavior. Pagination support (or a higher cap) is needed on the public page, not just the admin page.

findings.title: {{#unless automatic}} checks the member's automatic flag, so the remove link always renders
findings.body: This template is rendered as the itemView of `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` in admin/templates/group.hbs, so its context is the member (a User), not the group. Users have no `automatic` property, so `automatic` is undefined and the `{{#unless automatic}}` guard always passes — the remove (×) link is rendered for members of automatic groups too. Clicking it triggers Admin::GroupsController#remove_member, which correctly rejects the request with a 422 (`can_not_modify_automatic`), and the client's `removeMember` action has no error handling, so the admin just gets a confusing failure. The template needs the group's flag (e.g. via the parent view/controller) instead of resolving `automatic` on the member.

findings.title: limit parameter on public members endpoint is unbounded
findings.body: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` accepts any value with no maximum, and this endpoint is reachable by any user who can see the group. A request with `limit=1000000` will load and serialize that many users in one request. The old code had the same flaw but only for automatic groups; it now applies to all groups. Clamp the limit (e.g. `[[limit, 200].min, 1].max`).

findings.title: remove_member spec uses PUT although the route is DELETE, and specs never exercise the real routes
findings.body: The spec calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...` but config/routes.rb wires `remove_member` to DELETE only. Controller specs bypass the router, so the test still passes — and for the same reason none of the add_members/remove_member specs detect that the actual routes supply the group id as `params[:id]` while the controller requires `params[:group_id]` (which makes the feature fail with a 400 in production). Use the correct verb and, ideally, add request/route-level specs that go through the router for these two endpoints.
